messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <finance@stellar-analytics.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Merchant entity traceback & withholding — missing payout details

Hi Logan,

We received our Nov payout and noticed a sizeable portion (~$42,700) was withheld on the AWS marketplace settlement. Attached is our payout extract (Stellar_invoice_202611_AWS.csv) and a quick note of the affected SKUs. Can you explain why funds were withheld and what entity this was routed to on your side? Our accounting needs a ledger-level trail for month-end.

Key asks:
- Which merchant/entity ID was used for the withheld portion?
- Reason code from marketplace (withholding vs tax hold vs duplicate)
- Expected timeline to release or apply credits to our account

We’d like an answer by EOD Thursday Pacific so we can close our books.

Thanks,
Priyanka Shah
Head of Finance | Stellar Analytics
finance@stellar-analytics.com

Hi Priyanka,

Thanks for flagging and sending the extract — we received the CSV. I'm looping in Revenue Ops (Kimberly) and Tax (Rishi) to perform a ledger trace. Initial plan:

1) Kimberly will reconcile marketplace usage against merchant IDs and provide a per-invoice mapping.
2) Rishi will confirm whether this was a platform-initiated withholding (tax/regulatory) or routing to a different merchant entity.
3) If withholding is incorrect, we will calculate a credit and propose a timeline for payout release.

Can you confirm the legal entity Stellar wants credited (US vs EMEA)? If you can share entity registration docs (VAT / tax forms), that will speed things up.

I’ll update you with a status by tomorrow afternoon.

— Logan

Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-02T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Merchant entity traceback & withholding — missing payout details

Logan / Rishi,

I ran the initial reconciliation against AWS and GCP marketplace ledgers. Findings (summary):

- AWS settlement lines: Two merchant IDs received usage for Stellar SKUs in Nov. Merchant ID A (mapped to Stellar US, 65% of usage) and Merchant ID B (mapped to Stellar EMEA, 35% of usage). The withheld $42,700 correlates exactly to lines billed under Merchant ID B.
- Marketplace reason: AWS flagged cross-entity routing to a non-US merchant and applied a regulatory withholding hold pending local tax info.
- GCP payout (sample) shows matching cross-entity routing for some SKUs; I attached the spreadsheet for the Q4 sample.

Next steps I recommend:
- Provide entity mapping CSV to Stellar so they can confirm which legal entity owns the revenue lines (attached: entity-mapping.csv).
- If Stellar confirms US entity owns all lines, we request they provide VAT/EIN/W-8 forms to clear the withholding.
- If EMEA entity is correct, we need to coordinate on withholding receipts so Stellar can claim a credit in their EU books.

I've attached GCP_metering_spreadsheet_Q4.xlsx and entity-mapping.csv for the lines I reviewed.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: GCP_metering_spreadsheet_Q4.xlsx; entity-mapping.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-03T10:40:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Merchant entity traceback & withholding — missing payout details

Team,

Thanks Kim — confirms what I expected. Quick note on the tax side: when marketplaces route billing to an entity outside the buyer’s jurisdiction, local fiscal authorities sometimes trigger withholding until the beneficiary provides proof of tax status. From our side, options are:

A) Stellar provides non-US tax forms (e.g., EU VAT registration or local tax certificate) that prove entitlement — marketplace can then release or reclassify the funds.
B) Redwood issues a compensating credit while Stellar collects withholding receipts from the marketplace; credit calculation attached (redwood_credit_calculation_202611.pdf).

If we go the credit route, we should:
- Apply a provisional credit for $42,700 to Stellar’s account (subject to evidence).
- Hold final settlement until Stellar provides withholding receipts; if the receipts show withholding was valid, we reverse/adjust the credit.

I’ll draft a short payment-release letter we can send to Stellar that outlines these steps.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Tax | Redwood Inference
Attachment: withholding_evidence.pdf (template of required receipts)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <finance@stellar-analytics.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Merchant entity traceback & withholding — missing payout details

Hi Priyanka,

Thanks for your patience — we traced the withheld lines to a mix of US and EMEA merchant IDs on the marketplace side (details attached). Two options to resolve quickly:

1) Provide entity confirmation + tax docs: If Stellar confirms the US entity should receive all revenue lines and can provide IRS/EIN or VAT registration (as applicable), marketplaces typically reclassify and release funds within 7–10 business days.

2) Interim credit from Redwood: We can apply a provisional credit of $42,700 to your Redwood account immediately, pending delivery of the marketplace withholding receipts. If the receipts show the withholding was valid, we’ll reconcile and adjust the credit. I attached our credit calc and a template of required withholding receipts for marketplace acceptance.

Requested next steps from Stellar:
- Confirm which legal entity should be credited for Nov usage (US or EMEA).
- Share any VAT / EIN / W-8BEN-E or local tax docs you can at your earliest convenience.
- If you prefer the intermediary credit, confirm in writing and we’ll apply the provisional credit by COB Monday PST.

We want to avoid a chargeback loop with the marketplace; getting the receipts will close this cleanly.

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_credit_calculation_202611.pdf; withholding_evidence.pdf
